findings.title: Zeus Usermode Rootkit — API Hooks in services.exe

peirce_chain.firstness: Inline/Trampoline hooks on ntdll.dll!NtCreateThread (0x7c90d7d2 → JMP 0x7e3b47) and ntdll.dll!NtQueryDirectoryFile in services.exe PID 676. Hook destination 0x7e3b47 is in unknown module — not mapped to any loaded DLL. Hook code establishes stack frame (PUSH EBP, MOV EBP ESP). Volatility zeus-apihooks plugin positive match.
peirce_chain.secondness: services.exe (Service Control Manager) should never have hooked ntdll functions. NtQueryDirectoryFile hook makes processes invisible to pslist/tasklist — active process hiding. NtCreateThread hook intercepts all thread creation system-wide for injection. Hook destination in unmapped memory is definitive Zeus usermode API-hook signature. 9/9 habit incongruence anomalies detected, 99% compromise probability. No legitimate security product hooks ntdll from unmapped memory regions.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Zeus banking trojan installed usermode rootkit in services.exe to: (1) hide its own processes from OS enumeration (NtQueryDirectoryFile), (2) intercept thread creation for code injection (NtCreateThread), (3) operate under SYSTEM privileges via services.exe PID 676. The hook-to-unmapped-memory pattern is the canonical Zeus signature: injected code exists only in process memory, never on disk, evading all file-based AV scanning. This is active concealment of malicious presence — the attacker is hiding that they are hiding.

findings.carnegie_pattern: Authority transfer via trusted system process (services.exe) — borrowing SYSTEM-level legitimacy to shield injected code
mitre_ttps: T1562.001 (Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools)
findings.devil_advocate: The ntdll hooks could be from a legitimate security product (HIPS, EDR, or kernel-mode AV). Some security tools hook NtCreateThread for behavioral monitoring. REFUTATION: (1) Legitimate security hooks resolve to mapped, signed DLLs — not unmapped memory at 0x7e3b47. (2) No security product hooks NtQueryDirectoryFile to hide processes — that is exclusively a rootkit function. (3) Hook code signature (PUSH EBP, MOV EBP ESP, JMP) matches known Zeus stub, not any commercial security product. (4) Volatility zeus-apihooks is a purpose-built detector with near-zero false positive rate on this hook pattern. (5) APT1 IOC set confirms match. Benign hypothesis fails on all structural tests.
findings.corroboration: ART-002 (shimcache) confirms a.exe persistence binary running every 65s from the same host — Zeus dropper maintaining persistence. ART-003 (event logs) confirms CertEnroll activity under infected session — credential theft while rootkit active.

shannon_entropy.interpretation: Normal text range for artifact descriptions. ART-002 slightly elevated (5.07) due to hex addresses and path encoding.

findings.title: Mechanical Persistence with AV Evasion — Dual-Path a.exe

peirce_chain.firstness: Binary a.exe executed every 65 seconds from C:\Users\VIBRAN~1\AppData\Local\Temp\a.exe (shimcachemem: 29 entries, 2012-04-06 20:25:30 to 20:52:56). Same binary at C:\Windows\TEMP\a.exe (shimcache disk: 20 entries, 2012-04-04 00:23:33 to 00:44:11). McAfee EntVUtil.EXE interleaved at position 12.
peirce_chain.secondness: 65-second execution interval with sigma < 1s is mechanical — no human operates at this regularity. Two different filesystem paths for identical binary name indicates self-copying persistence to survive partial cleanup. VIBRAN~1 is 8.3 truncation of the executive’s profile path. McAfee AV running but unable to detect or terminate the persistence — AV evasion confirmed. The disk shimcache timestamps (April 4) predate the memory shimcache timestamps (April 6) by 2 days, indicating the malware survived at least one system restart.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Deliberate persistence mechanism designed to: (1) survive partial cleanup by maintaining copies in both user temp and system temp, (2) evade AV detection despite McAfee actively scanning (AV evasion), (3) maintain 65-second beacon interval for C2 communication or payload refresh. The dual-path strategy and AV coexistence indicate operational sophistication beyond opportunistic malware. The 2-day disk-to-memory gap confirms the persistence mechanism survived system restarts.

findings.carnegie_pattern: AV evasion — coexisting with McAfee without triggering detection
findings.devil_advocate: a.exe could be a legitimate scheduled task or system maintenance utility. Some enterprise tools run at fixed intervals from temp directories. REFUTATION: (1) No legitimate utility is named 'a.exe' — this is deliberately minimal to avoid pattern-matching. (2) No legitimate tool copies itself between user and system temp directories. (3) 65-second interval is not a standard Windows Task Scheduler interval. (4) The binary coexists with McAfee but is not detected — consistent with packed/obfuscated malware, not a signed enterprise tool. (5) The shimcache exec_flag confirms actual execution, not mere presence.
findings.corroboration: ART-001 (Zeus hooks) confirms the host is compromised by Zeus banking trojan — a.exe is the persistence component of the same infection chain.

human_jitter.tool_note: Tool returned NOISE (CV=0.1591 above automation threshold due to final 13s interval inflating variance). However, raw intervals are definitively mechanical. See KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.

findings.title: Certificate Theft via CertEnroll under Zeus Session

peirce_chain.firstness: CertEnroll Events 64/65 for nromanoff at 05:52:06Z, 13:52:08Z, 20:25:38Z. Same CertEnroll GUID {FF4EC912-3049-4750-BF0F-76264AB0DC15} appears for rsydow at 20:25:37Z and 20:37:59Z. Group Policy Event 5017 confirms CN=Natasha Romanoff, OU=Executives, DC=shieldbase, DC=local.
peirce_chain.secondness: rsydow authenticates on the same workstation 1 second before nromanoff CertEnroll at 20:25 — this temporal correlation is too tight for coincidence. Certificate enrollment under an active Zeus session means the private key material is exposed to the rootkit’s memory-resident hooks. The CertEnroll GUID reuse between two users suggests either credential relay or session hijack. The target is in OU=Executives — high-value certificates for lateral movement.
peirce_chain.thirdness: The Zeus trojan intercepted certificate enrollment for an executive-level account, exposing private key material to the attacker. The rsydow authentication 1 second before the CertEnroll event suggests the attacker used lateral movement credentials to trigger certificate operations on the compromised workstation. This enables PKI-based lateral movement: stolen executive certificates authenticate to domain resources without passwords.

findings.carnegie_pattern: None — automated credential theft, no social engineering component
findings.devil_advocate: rsydow could be a legitimate IT administrator performing certificate maintenance on the executive’s workstation. CertEnroll events are normal during PKI operations. The 1-second gap could be coincidental. PARTIAL ACCEPTANCE: rsydow is identified as a legitimate user in the SRL-2018 corpus (appears in DMZ-FTP case as DFIR analyst). However: (1) The 1-second temporal correlation between rsydow login and nromanoff CertEnroll is operationally suspicious regardless of rsydow’s legitimacy. (2) The CertEnroll occurs under an active Zeus infection — any certificate operation exposes key material to the rootkit. (3) The same GUID shared between users is anomalous for independent certificate operations. Verdict maintained at INTENT, not MALICE, because rsydow’s access may be legitimate DFIR activity on the infected host.
findings.corroboration: ART-001 (Zeus hooks) confirms the rootkit was active during CertEnroll. ART-002 (a.exe) confirms ongoing malware activity on the same host.

findings.title: Potential C2 Channel via Twitter Image Steganography

peirce_chain.firstness: IE cache contains Twitter profile images from a0.twimg.com: _ndice_normal[1].jpg (762 bytes) and 336922595_normal[1].jpg (825 bytes) in cache directory 201RVRNG. Access times: 2012-04-03T00:25:29Z and 08:34:03Z — approximately 8 hours apart.
peirce_chain.secondness: Zeus variants are documented to use Twitter profile images for C2 steganography (MITRE T1102). Two profile images fetched at an 8-hour interval is consistent with periodic C2 beaconing. The _ndice_normal filename suggests a non-English profile (underscore replacing accented character — likely índice), consistent with Zeus botnet infrastructure using compromised Spanish/Portuguese accounts. However, normal web browsing also produces Twitter image cache entries.
peirce_chain.thirdness: The 8-hour beaconing interval and Zeus-infected host context make C2 steganography plausible. However, this is a single-source finding (IE cache only) with no packet capture or DNS log corroboration. The images could be legitimate Twitter browsing by the user. Rated SUSPICION per Daubert single-source standard.

findings.devil_advocate: Natasha Romanoff may have browsed Twitter legitimately. The 8-hour gap could correspond to work-start and lunch-break browsing. Profile images are fetched automatically by the Twitter web interface. PARTIAL ACCEPTANCE: This is plausible for the cache entries alone. The Zeus infection on the host increases the probability of C2 activity, but no direct evidence links these specific images to Zeus C2 functions. Downgraded to SUSPICION rather than INTENT due to single-source limitation.
findings.corroboration: Single source. No packet capture or DNS log independently confirms C2 function.
